transcript.content: Hello, I’m glad you came in. What brings you in today?

I go out of my way to avoid anything that reminds me of what happened to my cousin, even if it means cutting out parts of my life. It has been a little over a year since he was killed in Guatemala, and I find myself pulling away from my community and everyday activities just to avoid the memories.
Since your cousin was killed, do you also have unwanted memories or nightmares about what happened, or feel on edge and easily startled?

Yes, I constantly get sudden, horrible memories during the day of my cousin in his coffin that make my chest tighten, and at night I'm woken up by vivid nightmares about buses or my family. I also feel incredibly jumpy and on edge, like I'm jumping out of my skin if someone walks up behind me at work or if a car backfires on the street.
Since this happened, have you felt numb or detached from other people, had trouble feeling positive emotions, or had any gaps in memory about the event?

Yes, I feel completely flat and disconnected from others, and I can't even feel genuine happiness when my daughter gets an award at school. I've also noticed big blank spots in my memory around the time we viewed his body and talked about the attack, even though I remember the rest of the trip clearly.
Did you personally witness the killing or see the body, or were you exposed to the event in another direct way?

I didn't witness the shooting itself because I was in New York and flew to Guatemala afterward. However, I was directly exposed to it when I viewed his body with my family, saw the crime scene footage on the news, and listened to my aunt describe the attack in graphic detail. Seeing him in that coffin and hearing those horrible details are the exact images that keep flashing back to me.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient meets criteria for post-traumatic stress disorder: exposure to a qualifying traumatic event involving the violent death of a close family member, followed by persistent intrusion symptoms (recurrent distressing memories, vivid nightmares, physiological distress), avoidance of reminders, negative mood/cognition changes (emotional numbing, detachment, inability to feel positive emotions, memory gaps), and hyperarousal (exaggerated startle/jumpiness). Symptoms have persisted for over one year and cause social/functional withdrawal.
